s.d: γλῶσσα, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for לָשׁוֹן ;] 1. the tongue, as the organ of speech: [[mark 7 33|Mrk.7:33, 35]] [[luke 1 64|Luk.1:64 16:24]], [[acts 2 26|Act.2:26]]" (LXX), [[romans 3 13|Rom.3:13]] (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), [[1-corinthians 14 9|1Co.14:9]], [[philippians 2 11|Php.2:11]], [[james 1 26|Jas.1:26 3:5, 6 8]], [[1-peter 3 10|1Pe.3:10]]" (LXX), 1Jo.3:18, [[revelation 16 10|Rev.16:10]]; of a tongue-like object, [[acts 2 3|Act.2:3.]] 2. a tongue, language: [[acts 2 11|Act.2:11;]] joined with φυλή, λαός, ἔθνος, frequently in pl., [[revelation 5 9|Rev.5:9 7:9 10:11 11:9 13:7 14:6 17:15]]; λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γ., [[acts 2 4|Act.2:4;]] γ. λαλεῖν καιναῖς, WH, txt. (RV, mg., omit καιναῖς), [[mark 16 17|Mrk.16:17;]] λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, γλώσσῃ (see ICC, ll. with; DB, iv, 793ff.), [[mark 16 17|Mrk.16:17]], WH, txt., R, mg., [[acts 10 46|Act.10:46 19:6]], [[1-corinthians 12 30|1Co.12:30 13:1]] 14:2, 4-6, 13, 18, 23, 27, 39; γλῶσσαι (= λόγοι ἐν γλώσσῃ, [[1-corinthians 14 19|1Co.14:19]]), [[1-corinthians 13 8|1Co.13:8 14:22]]; γένη γλωσσῶν, [[1-corinthians 12 10|1Co.12:10, 28]]; προσεύχεσθαι γλώσσῃ, [[1-corinthians 14 14|1Co.14:14;]] γλῶσσαν ἔχειν, [[1-corinthians 14 26|1Co.14:26]] (Cremer, 163, 679). † (AS)

γλωσσόκομον, -ου, τό, vernac. form of cl. γλωσσοκομεῖον (γλῶσσα, κομέω), [in LXX for אָרוֹן, [[2-kings 6 11|2Ki.6:11]], [[2-chronicles 24 8|2Ch.24:8, 10 11]] * ;] 1. = cl. -εῖον (see supr.), a case for holding the reeds or tongues of musical instruments. 2. As in LXX, π. (MM, see word), a box, chest: [[john 12 6|Jhn.12:6 13:29]]. † (AS)
γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς (κνάπτω, to card wool), [in LXX for כָּבַס, 4Ki.18:17, [[isaiah 7 3|Isa.7:3 36:2]] * ;] a fuller, cloth-dresser: [[mark 9 3|Mrk.9:3.]]† (AS)

γνήσιος, -α, -ον (γίγνομαι), [in LXX: Sir.7:18, 3Ma.3:19 * ;] 1. prop., lawfully begotten, born in wedlock (in π., γυνὴ γ., a lawful wife; MM, see word). 2. true, genuine, sincere: [[philippians 4 3|Php.4:3]], [[1-timothy 1 2|1Ti.1:2]], [[titus 1 4|Tit.1:4]]; as subst., τὸ γ. = ἡ γνησιότης, sincerity, [[2-corinthians 8 8|2Co.8:8.]] † (AS)
γνησίως, adv., [in LXX: 2Ma.14:8, 3Ma.3:23 * ;] sincerely, honourably: [[philippians 2 20|Phi 2:20]] (for a parallel in π., see MM, see word).† (AS)

γνόφος (later form of δν-), [in LXX for אָפֵל, עֲרָפֶל, etc. ;] darkness, gloom (including "an element of tempest," Tr., Syn., §with): [[hebrews 12 18|Heb.12:18.]]† SYN.: ἀχλύς, ζόφος, σκότος (Tr., l.with; DB, i, 457a). (AS)

γνώμη, -ης, ἡ (γιγνώσκω), [in LXX: [[daniel 2 15|Da TH 2:15]] (דָּת), [[psalms 83 3|Ps 82(83):3]] (סוֹד), elsewhere, chiefly II Es, for טְעֵם ;] 1. a means of knowing, a token (Theogn.). 2. In Attic writers, the mind, its operations and results (see Edwards, Lex., App., A); (a) mind, understanding; (b) purpose, intention: [[acts 20 3|Act.20:3;]] (with) judgment, opinion: [[1-corinthians 1 10|1Co.1:10]], [[revelation 17 13|Rev.17:13]]; (d) counsel, advice: [[1-corinthians 7 25|1Co.7:25, 40]] [[2-corinthians 8 10|2Co.8:10]], Phm 14; (e) royal purpose, decree (as in Da, I and II Es): [[revelation 17 17|Rev.17:17]] (Cremer, 671). † (AS)

γνωρίζω (γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for ידע hi. ;] 1. as most commonly in cl., to come to know, discover, know: [[philippians 1 22|Php.1:22]] (but cf. R, mg.). 2. to make known: with accusative, [[romans 9 22|Rom.9:22, 23]]; with accusative of thing(s) da.t. of person(s), [[luke 2 15|Luk.2:15]], [[john 15 15|Jhn.15:15 17:26]], [[acts 2 28|Act.2:28]]" (LXX), [[1-corinthians 15 1|1Co.15:1]], [[2-corinthians 8 1|2Co.8:1]], [[galatians 1 11|Gal.1:11]], [[ephesians 1 9|Eph.1:9 6:19, 21]] [[colossians 4 7|Col.4:7]], 9 [[2-peter 1 16|2Pe.1:16]]; with dative, before ὅτι, [[1-corinthians 12 3|1Co.12:3;]] before τί, [[colossians 1 27|Col.1:27;]] περί, [[luke 2 17|Luk.2:17.]] Pass., [[acts 7 13|Act.7:13]], [[romans 16 26|Rom.16:26]], [[ephesians 3 3|Eph.3:3]], 6 10, [[philippians 4 6|Php.4:6]] (Cremer, 677; cf. ἀνα-, δια-γνωρίζω). † (AS)

γνῶσις, -εως, ἡ (γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for דַּעַת ;] 1. a seeking to know, inquiry, investigation. 2. knowledge, in NT, specially of the kn. of spiritual truth: absol., [[luke 11 52|Luk.11:52]], [[romans 2 20|Rom.2:20 15:14]], [[1-corinthians 1 5|1Co.1:5]] (Lft., Notes, 147) 8:1, 7, 10, 11, 13:2, 8 14:6, [[2-corinthians 6 6|2Co.6:6 8:7 11:6]], [[ephesians 3 19|Eph.3:19]], [[colossians 2 3|Col.2:3]], [[1-peter 3 7|1Pe.3:7]], [[2-peter 1 5|2Pe.1:5]], 6; with genitive obj., σωτηρίας, [[luke 1 77|Luk.1:77;]] τ. δόξης τ. θεοῦ, [[2-corinthians 4 6|2Co.4:6;]] τ. θεοῦ, [[2-corinthians 2 14|2Co.2:14 10:5]]; Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, [[philippians 3 8|Php.3:8]] (see Deiss., LAE, 383.8), [[2-peter 3 18|2Pe.3:18;]] with genitive subjc., θεοῦ, [[romans 11 33|Rom.11:33;]] λόγος γνώσεως, [[1-corinthians 12 8|1Co.12:8;]] ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως, [[1-timothy 6 20|1Ti.6:20.]] † SYN.: σοφία, φρόνησις (cf. ἐπί-γνωσις and see Lft. on [[colossians 2 3|Col.2:3;]] Cremer, 156). (AS)
γνώστης, -ου, ὁ (γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for יִדְּעֹנִי ;] one who knows, an expert: [[acts 26 3|Act.26:3.]]† (AS)

γνωστός, -ή, -όν, later form of γνωστός (γιγνώσκω), [in LXX for various parts of ידע ;] known: [[acts 9 42|Act.9:42;]] with dative, [[john 18 15|Jhn.18:15, 16]] (Rec.), [[acts 1 19|Act.1:19 2:14 4:10 13:38 15:18 19:17 28:22, 28]]; γ. σημεῖον, a notable (EV) sign, one that is matter of knowledge, [[acts 4 16|Act.4:16;]] γνωστὸν, [[acts 15 17|Act.15:17, 18]]; τὸ γνωστὸν θεοῦ, [[romans 1 19|Rom.1:19;]] in pl., as subst., γνωστοί, acquaintances, [[luke 2 44|Luk.2:44 23:49]]; so in sing., [[john 18 16|Jhn.18:16]] (WH).† (AS)

γογγύζω, [in LXX chiefly for לוּן ;] to mutter, murmur: [[1-corinthians 10 10|1Co.10:10;]] before κατά, [[matthew 20 11|Mat.20:11;]] πρός, [[luke 5 30|Luk.5:30;]] περί, [[john 6 41|Jhn.6:41, 61]]; μετ᾽ ἀλλήλων, [[john 6 43|Jhn.6:43;]] with accusative, before περί, [[john 7 32|Jhn.7:32]] (cf. δια-γογγύζω).† (AS)

γογγυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: [[isaiah 58 9|Isa.58:9]] (אָוֶן), [[exodus 16 7|Exo.16:7-9]], [[numbers 17 5|Num.17:5, 10]] (תְּלוּנָה), Wis.1:10, 11 Sir.46:7 * ;] a murmuring, muttering: [[john 7 12|Jhn.7:12]], [[acts 6 1|Act.6:1]]; ἄνευ γ., [[1-peter 4 9|1Pe.4:9;]] pl., χωρὶς γ., [[philippians 2 14|Php.2:14.]]† (AS)
γογγυστής, -οῦ, ὁ (γογγύζω); [in Sm.: [[proverbs 26 22|Pro.26:22]], [[isaiah 29 24|Isa.29:24]]; Th.: [[proverbs 26 20|Pro.26:20]] * ;] a murmurer: Ju 16.† (AS)
γόης, -ητος, ὁ (γοάω, to wail), 1. a wailer. 2. a wizard. 3. an impostor (cf. γοητεία, trickery, 2Ma.12:24): [[2-timothy 3 13|2Ti.3:13]]. † (AS)

Γολγοθά (Rec. -θᾶ; WH, mg., Γολγόθ, Jo, l.with, Aram. גָּלְגָּלְתָּא = Heb. גֻּלְגֹּלֶת, LXX, κρανίον, [[judges 9 53|Jdg.9:53]], [[2-samuel 9 35|2Ki.9:35]]); indecl. (exc. [[mark 15 22|Mrk.15:22]], -άν), Golgotha, the place of the crucifixion: [[matthew 27 33|Mat.27:33]], [[mark 15 22|Mrk.15:22]], [[john 19 17|Jhn.19:17]].† (AS)
Γόμορρα, -ας, ἡ, and -ων, τά (Heb. עֲמֹרָה), Gomorrah, one of the cities of the plain (Gen.19): [[matthew 10 15|Mat.10:15]], [[romans 9 29|Rom.9:29]]" (LXX), [[2-peter 2 6|2Pe.2:6]], Ju 7.† (AS)
γόμος, -ου, ὁ (γέμω), [in LXX: [[exodus 23 5|Exo.23:5]], [[2-kings 5 17|4Ki.5:17]] (מַשָּׂא) * ;] a ship's freight, cargo: [[acts 21 3|Act.21:3]], [[revelation 18 11|Rev.18:11, 12]].† (AS)

γονεύς, -έως, ὁ (γίγνομαι), [in LXX for אָב, אֵם ;] a begetter, a father; mostly in pl., οἱ γ., parents: [[luke 2 41|Luk.2:41, 43 8:56 21:16]], [[john 9 2|Jhn.9:2, 3 20, 22, 23]] [[romans 1 30|Rom.1:30]], [[2-corinthians 12 14|2Co.12:14]], [[ephesians 6 1|Eph.6:1]], [[colossians 3 20|Col.3:20]], [[2-timothy 3 2|2Ti.3:2]]; accusative pl. (Hellenistic, see Thackeray, Gr., i, 148), γονεῖς, [[matthew 10 21|Mat.10:21]], [[mark 13 22|Mrk.13:22]], [[luke 2 27|Luk.2:27 18:29]], [[john 9 18|Jhn.9:18]].† (AS)

γόνυ, -ατος, τό, [in LXX chiefly for בֶּרֶךְ ;] the knee: [[hebrews 12 12|Heb.12:12;]] of a suppliant, προσπίπτειν τοῖς γ., [[luke 5 8|Luk.5:8;]] so also τιθέναι τὰ γ., to kneel: [[luke 22 41|Luk.22:41]], [[acts 7 60|Act.7:60 9:40 20:36 21:5]]; in mockery, [[mark 15 19|Mrk.15:19;]] κάμπτειν τὰ γ., to bend the knee: [[romans 11 4|Rom.11:4]] (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), [[ephesians 3 14|Eph.3:14]], [[philippians 2 10|Php.2:10]].† (AS)

γονυπετέω, -ῶ) (γόνυ, πίπτω); 1. to fall on the knees: before ἔμπροσθεν, [[matthew 27 29|Mat.27:29.]] 2. to fall down before one: with accusative, [[matthew 17 14|Mat.17:14]], [[mark 1 40|Mrk.1:40]], R, txt., 10:17. † (AS)

γράμμα, -τος, τό (γράφω), [in LXX for סֵפֶר, etc. ;] 1. that which is traced or drawn, a picture. 2. that which is written; (1) a character, letter: [[galatians 6 11|Gal.6:11;]] (2) a writing, a written document; (a) a bill or account: [[luke 16 6|Luk.16:6]], 7; (b) a letter: [[acts 28 21|Act.28:21;]] (with) τὰ ἱερὰ γ., the sacred writings, i.e. the OT: [[2-timothy 3 15|2Ti.3:15]] (so in Philo, Vit. Mos., iii, 39) ; (d) τὸ γ., the letter, the written word as an external authority in contrast with the direct influence of the Spirit as manifested in the new Covenant: [[romans 2 27|Rom.2:27, 29 7:6]], [[2-corinthians 3 6|2Co.3:6]], 7; (3) τὰ γ., letters, i.e. learning: [[john 7 15|Jhn.7:15]], [[acts 26 24|Act.26:24]]. (In π. an illiterate person is very frequently referred to as γράμματα μ᾽̀ εἰδότης, and this "never means anything else than inability to write": MM, Exp., x; but see also Cremer, 166; DCG, i, 202; ii, 584.) † (AS)

γραμματεύς, -έως (accusative pl., -εῖς, see Bl., §8, 2), ὁ (γράμμα), [in LXX always for שׁטר in Hex., elsewhere chiefly for ספר ;] 1. a secretary; γ. τ. πόλεως, a state-clerk: [[acts 19 35|Act.19:35.]] 2. In π., of a military officer (Deiss., BS, 110f.). So [[judges 5 14|Jdg.5:14]], [[2-kings 25 19|4Ki.25:19]] (ספר), al. 3. a scribe, a biblical scholar, teacher of the law (so first in I [[esther 8 3|Est.8:3]], II [[esther 7 6|Est.7:6]]; in [[luke 5 17|Luk.5:17]], νομοδιδάσκαλος; in [[luke 10 25|Luk.10:25]], νομικός): [[matthew 7 29|Mat.7:29]], [[mark 1 22|Mrk.1:22]], and frequently in Gosp. γ. καὶ ἀρχιερεῖς, [[matthew 2 4|Mat.2:4]], and al.; γ. κ. Φαρισαῖοι, [[matthew 5 20|Mat.5:20]], and al.; γ. μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τ. οὐρ., [[matthew 13 52|Mat.13:52;]] ποῦ σοφός; ποῦ γ., [[1-corinthians 1 20|1Co.1:20]] (Cremer, 167; DB, iv, 420, 800). (AS)
γραπτός, -ή, -όν (γράφω), [in LXX for מִכְתָּב ;] 1. painted. 2. written: [[romans 2 15|Rom.2:15.]] † (AS)

γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (γράφω), [in LXX chiefly for כְּתָב ;] 1. a drawing, painting. 2. (a) writing; (b) that which is written, a writing: πᾶσα γ., [[2-timothy 3 16|2Ti.3:16;]] γ. ἅγιαι, [[romans 1 2|Rom.1:2;]] προφητικαί, [[romans 16 26|Rom.16:26;]] al αἱ γ. τ. προφητῶν, [[matthew 26 56|Mat.26:56;]] ἡ γ., αἱ γ., the sacred writings, the Scriptures (i.e. the OT; see Milligan, NTD, 205); in pl., when the sacred writings as a whole are meant, e.g. [[matthew 21 42|Mat.21:42 26:54]], [[john 5 39|Jhn.5:39]], [[romans 15 4|Rom.15:4]]; in sing., when a particular passage is referred to, as in [[luke 4 21|Luk.4:21]], [[john 19 24|Jhn.19:24]], [[romans 4 3|Rom.4:3 9:17 10:11 11:2]], [[james 2 23|Jas.2:23]] (Cremer, 165; DCG, ii, 584). (AS)

γράφω, [in LXX chiefly for כּתב ]; 1. to scrape, graze (Hom.), and later (Hdt.) to sketch, draw. 2. to write; (a) of forming or tracing letters on writing material: Jhn.8:[6], [[galatians 6 11|Gal.6:11]], [[2-thessalonians 3 17|2Th.3:17]]; (b) to express in writing, commit to writing, record: [[luke 1 63|Luk.1:63]], [[john 19 21|Jhn.19:21, 22]] [[revelation 1 11|Rev.1:11, 19]] al.; of scripture as a standing authority (Deiss., BS, 112ff.), γέγραπται, it stands written (Luther), [[matthew 4 4|Mat.4:4]], [[mark 7 6|Mrk.7:6]], [[luke 4 8|Luk.4:8]], [[romans 1 17|Rom.1:17]], [[1-corinthians 1 31|1Co.1:31]], al.; id. before ἐν, [[mark 1 2|Mrk.1:2]], [[acts 1 20|Act.1:20]], al.; with accusative, to write of: [[john 1 46|Jhn.1:46]], [[romans 10 5|Rom.10:5]]; before περί, [[matthew 26 24|Mat.26:24]], [[mark 14 21|Mrk.14:21]], [[john 5 46|Jhn.5:46;]] al.; with dative (WM, §31, 4), [[luke 18 31|Luk.18:31;]] id. before ἵνα (M, Pr., 207f.), [[mark 12 19|Mrk.12:19]], [[luke 20 28|Luk.20:28]]; κατὰ τ. γεγραμμένον, [[2-corinthians 4 13|2Co.4:13;]] γεγραμμένον ἐστί, [[john 2 17|Jhn.2:17;]] ἐγράφη, [[romans 4 24|Rom.4:24;]] ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ γεγραμμένα, [[john 12 16|Jhn.12:16;]] (with) of writing directions or information, with dative of person(s): [[romans 15 15|Rom.15:15]], [[2-corinthians 7 12|2Co.7:12]], al.; (d) of that which contains the record or message: βιβλίον, [[mark 10 4|Mrk.10:4]], [[john 21 25|Jhn.21:25]], [[revelation 5 1|Rev.5:1]]; τίτλον, [[john 19 19|Jhn.19:19;]] ἐπιστολήν, [[acts 23 25|Act.23:25;]] ἐντολήν, [[mark 10 5|Mrk.10:5]] (cf. ἀπο-, ἐγ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, προ-). (AS)
γραώδης, -ες (γραῦς, an old woman, εἶδος), anile, old-womanish: [[1-timothy 4 7|1Ti.4:7.]]† (AS)

γρηγορέω, -ῶ, = Attic ἐργήγορα, pf. of ἐγείρω, which see, [in LXX (later bks. only) chiefly for שׁקד ;] 1. to be awake; metaphorically, of being alive, [[1-thessalonians 5 10|1Th.5:10.]] 2. to watch: [[matthew 24 43|Mat.24:43 26:38, 40]] [[mark 13 34|Mrk.13:34 14:34, 37]] [[luke 12 37|Luk.12:37]], 39; metaphorically, [[matthew 24 42|Mat.24:42 25:13 26:41]], [[mark 13 35|Mrk.13:35]], 37 14:38, [[acts 20 31|Act.20:31]], [[1-corinthians 16 13|1Co.16:13]], [[1-thessalonians 5 6|1Th.5:6]], [[1-peter 5 8|1Pe.5:8]], [[revelation 3 2|Rev.3:2, 3 16:15]]; before ἐν, [[colossians 4 2|Col.4:2.]] (Cf. δια-γρηγορέω).† SYN.: see: ἀγρθπνέω. (AS)

γυμνάζω (γυμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.10:15 * ;] 1. properly, to exercise naked. 2. Generally, to exercise, train the body or mind: [[1-timothy 4 7|1Ti.4:7]], [[hebrews 5 14|Heb.5:14 12:11]], [[2-peter 2 14|2Pe.2:14]]. † (AS)
γυμνασία, -ας, ἡ (γυμνάζω), [in LXX: 4Ma.11:20 * ;] exercise: [[1-timothy 4 8|1Ti.4:8.]]† (AS)

γυμνιτεύω (Rec. γυμνητ-, V. Tdf ., Pr., 81), to be naked or scantily clad: [[1-corinthians 4 11|1Co.4:11]] (cf. ἐν ψύχει κ. γυμνότητι), [[2-corinthians 11 27|2Co.11:27;]] γυμνοί, [[james 2 15|Jas.2:15.]] In κοινή writers, γ. also means to go light-armed.† (AS)

γυμνός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX chiefly for עָרוֹם ;] naked, without clothing, and sometimes (as frequently in cl.) scantily or poorly clad ([[isaiah 20 2|Isa.20:2]]ff., Tob.1:16, 2Ma.11:12): [[matthew 25 36|Mat.25:36, 38 43, 44]], [[mark 14 52|Mrk.14:52]], [[john 21 7|Jhn.21:7]], [[acts 19 16|Act.19:16]], [[james 2 15|Jas.2:15]], [[revelation 3 17|Rev.3:17 16:15, 17:16]]; as subst., to γ., the naked body, [[mark 14 51|Mrk.14:51.]] Metaphorical, of things exposed, [[hebrews 4 13|Heb.4:13;]] of the soul without a body (Plat., Crat., with, 20, and cf. Deiss., LAE, 293), [[2-corinthians 5 3|2Co.5:3;]] of seed, bare, [[1-corinthians 15 37|1Co.15:37]] (Cremer, 168).† (AS)
γυμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (γυμνός), [in LXX for עֵירֹם, [[deuteronomy 28 48|Deu.28:48]] * ;] nakedness: [[romans 8 35|Rom.8:35]], [[2-corinthians 11 27|2Co.11:27]], [[revelation 3 18|Rev.3:18]].† (AS)
γυναικάριον, -ου, τό (diminutive of γυνή), a little woman; contemptuously, a silly woman (EV): [[2-timothy 3 6|2Ti.3:6.]]† (AS)
γυναικεῖος, -α, -ον (γυνή), [in LXX chiefly for אִשָּׁה ;] female: [[1-peter 3 7|1Pe.3:7.]]† (AS)

γυνή, -αικός, ἡ, [in LXX for אִשָּׁה ;] 1. a woman, married or unmarried: [[matthew 11 11|Mat.11:11 14:21]], al.; ὕπανδρος γ., [[romans 7 2|Rom.7:2;]] γ. χήρα, [[luke 4 26|Luk.4:26;]] in vocat., γύναι implies neither reproof nor severity, but is used frequently as a term of respect and endearment, [[matthew 15 28|Mat.15:28]], [[john 2 4|Jhn.2:4, 4:21 19:26]]. 2. a wife: [[matthew 1 20|Mat.1:20]], [[1-corinthians 7 3|1Co.7:3]], 4 al.; γ. ἀπολύειν, [[mark 10 2|Mrk.10:2]], al.; γ. ἔχειν [[mark 6 18|Mrk.6:18;]] γ. λαβεῖν, [[mark 12 19|Mrk.12:19;]] γ. γαμεῖν, [[luke 14 20|Luk.14:20.]] 3. a deaconess, [[1-timothy 3 11|1Ti.3:11]] (CGT, in l.). (AS)

γυνή, -αικός, ἡ, [in LXX for אִשָּׁה ;] 1. a woman, married or unmarried: [[matthew 11 11|Mat.11:11 14:21]], al.; ὕπανδρος γ., [[romans 7 2|Rom.7:2;]] γ. χήρα, [[luke 4 26|Luk.4:26;]] in vocat., γύναι implies neither reproof nor severity, but is used frequently as a term of respect and endearment, [[matthew 15 28|Mat.15:28]], [[john 2 4|Jhn.2:4, 4:21 19:26]]. 2. a wife: [[matthew 1 20|Mat.1:20]], [[1-corinthians 7 3|1Co.7:3]], 4 al.; γ. ἀπολύειν, [[mark 10 2|Mrk.10:2]], al.; γ. ἔχειν [[mark 6 18|Mrk.6:18;]] γ. λαβεῖν, [[mark 12 19|Mrk.12:19;]] γ. γαμεῖν, [[luke 14 20|Luk.14:20.]] 3. a deaconess, [[1-timothy 3 11|1Ti.3:11]] (CGT, in l.). (AS)
Γώγ, ὁ (Heb. גּוֹג), indecl., Gog, assoc. with Magog (q.v): [[revelation 20 8|Rev.20:8.]]† (AS)

γωνία, -ας, ἡ (γόνυ), [in LXX chiefly for פִּנָּה ;] an angle, a corner: [[matthew 6 5|Mat.6:5]], [[acts 26 26|Act.26:26]]; τ. τέσσαρας γ. τ. γῆς, [[revelation 7 1|Rev.7:1, 20:8]]; κεφαλὴ γνωνίας (רֹאשׁ פִּנָּה, [[psalms 118 22|Ps 117(118):22]], LXX), [[matthew 21 42|Mat.21:42]], [[mark 12 10|Mrk.12:10]], [[luke 20 17|Luk.20:17]], [[acts 4 11|Act.4:11]], [[1-peter 2 7|1Pe.2:7]].† (AS)

Δαυείδ (Rec. Δαβίδ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּוִד), David, King of Israel: [[matthew 1 6|Mat.1:6; 12:3]], and al.; σκηνὴ Δ., [[acts 15 16|Act.15:16;]] κλεὶς Δ., [[revelation 3 7|Rev.3:7;]] θρόνος Δ., [[luke 1 32|Luk.1:32;]] ῥίζα Δ., [[revelation 5 5|Rev.5:5;]] βασιλεία Δ., [[mark 11 10|Mrk.11:10;]] υἱὸς Δ., the Messiah (Ps. Sol., 17:23; for other reff. in Jewish lit., see Dalman, Words, 317), [[matthew 1 1|Mat.1:1 9:27]], and al.; ἐν Δ., i.e. the Psalter, [[hebrews 4 7|Heb.4:7]] (AS)

δαιμονίζομαι (in cl. also δαιμονάω; δαίμων), [in Aq.: [[psalms 91 6|Ps 90(91):6]] * ;] to be under the power of a δαίμων (δαιμόνιον, which see), to be possessed: [[matthew 15 22|Mat.15:22;]] elsewhere always ptcp., -ιζόμενος, -ισθείς: [[matthew 4 24|Mat.4:24; 8:16, 28, 33 9:32 12:22]], [[mark 1 32|Mrk.1:32 15 16 18]], [[luke 8 36|Luk.8:36]], [[john 10 21|Jhn.10:21]] (Cremer, 171).† (AS)

δαιμόνιον, -ου, τό (neut. of δαιμόνιος, -α, -ον, divine), [in LXX (so also in π; see MM, Exp., x) for שֵׁד, אֱלִיל, (frequently in To) ;] 1. as in cl.; (a) the Divine power, Deity (Hdt., Plat., al.); (b) an inferior divinity, deity or demon (as in magical π, Deiss., BS, 281; MM, Exp., x): ξένα δ., [[acts 17 18|Act.17:18.]] 2. (a) in OT, heathen deities, false gods (e.g. [[deuteronomy 32 17|Deu.32:17]], Psa.95 (96):5); (b) in NT, evil spirits, demons: θύουσιν δαιμονίοις, [[1-corinthians 10 20|1Co.10:20;]] διδασκαλίαι δαιμονίων, [[1-timothy 4 1|1Ti.4:1;]] προσκυνεῖν τὰ δ., [[revelation 9 20|Rev.9:20;]] ἄρχων τῶν δ., [[matthew 9 34|Mat.9:34;]] especially (syn. with πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον) as operating upon and "possessing" (of. δαιμονίζομαι) men: [[matthew 11 18|Mat.11:18]], and al.; εἰσέρχεσθαι δ. εἰς. . ., [[luke 8 30|Luk.8:30;]] δ. ἔχειν, [[luke 4 33|Luk.4:33;]] δ. ἐκβάλλειν, [[matthew 7 22|Mat.7:22]] In the phrase πνεῦμα δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, [[luke 4 33|Luk.4:33]], the wider cl. usage (1. b) is recognised, ἀκ. being elsewhere in NT, the epithet of πν., and δ. = πν. ἀκ. (see ICC, in l; Cremer, 168) (AS)
δαιμονιώδης, -ες (δαιμόνιον, εἶδος), [in Sm.: [[psalms 91 6|Ps 90(91):6]] * ;] demon-like: [[james 3 15|Jas.3:15]] (Cremer, 171).† (AS)
δαίμων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX for גַּד, [[isaiah 65 11|Isa.65:11]] (א; δαιμονίῳ, AB) * ;] in cl. and NT = δαιμόνιον; a demon: [[matthew 8 31|Mat.8:31.]]† (AS)
δάκνω [in LXX for נשׁךְ, [[genesis 49 17|Gen.49:17]], al., exc. [[deuteronomy 8 15|Deu.8:15]] (שׂרף) ;] to bite: metaphorically, [[galatians 5 15|Gal.5:15.]]† (AS)

δάκρυον (poët. form δάκρυ), -ου, τό, [in LXX for דִּמְעָה ;] a tear: [[mark 9 24|Mrk.9:24]] (WH, txt., R, txt. omit), [[acts 20 19|Act.20:19, 31]], [[2-corinthians 2 4|2Co.2:4]], [[2-timothy 1 4|2Ti.1:4]], [[hebrews 5 7|Heb.5:7 12:17]], [[revelation 7 17|Rev.7:17 21:4]]; metaphorically, dative pl., δάκρυσι ([[lamentations 2 11|La 2:11]], Thuc., vii, 75; Bl., § 9, 3), [[luke 7 38|Luk.7:38, 44]].† (AS)

δακρύω [in LXX for בָּכָה, etc. ;] to weep, shed tears: [[john 11 35|Jhn.11:35.]]† SYN.: κλαίω, of audible weeping, to cry; ὀδύρομαι, of grief expressed verbally, to lament; θρηνέω, of formal lamentation, to sing a dirge; ἀλαλάζω, to wail in Oriental fashion; στενάζω, of grief expressed by inarticulate sounds, to groan. (AS)
δακτύλιος, -ου, ὁ (δάκτυλος), [in LXX chiefly for טַבַּעַת ;] a ring: [[luke 15 22|Luk.15:22.]]† (AS)

δάκτυλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for אֶצְבַּע ;] a finger: [[matthew 23 4|Mat.23:4]], [[mark 7 33|Mrk.7:33]], [[luke 11 46|Luk.11:46 16:24]], [[john 8 6|Jhn.8:6, 8 20:25, 27]]; metaphorically, δ. θεοῦ (cf. [[exodus 8 19|Exo.8:19]]), [[luke 11 20|Luk.11:20]].† (AS)
Δαλμανουθά, ἡ indecl., Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee: [[mark 8 10|Mrk.8:10]] (cf. Μαγαδάν).† (AS)
Δαλματία (L, Δελ-), -ας, ἡ Dalmatia, a part of Illyria on E. coast of the Adriatic: [[2-timothy 4 10|2Ti.4:10.]]† (AS)
δαμάζω [in LXX: [[daniel 2 40|Dan.2:40]] (חֲשַׁל) * ;] to tame, subdue: [[mark 5 4|Mrk.5:4]], [[james 3 7|Jas.3:7]]; metaphorically, τ. γλῶσσαν, [[james 3 8|Jas.3:8]] (Field, Notes, 237f.).† (AS)
δάμαλις, -εως, ἡ (fem. of δαμάλης, a bullock), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָה, עֶגְלָה ;] a heifer, [[hebrews 9 13|Heb.9:13.]]† (AS)
Δάμαρις, -ιδος, ἡ (δάμαρ, poët., a wife), Damaris: [[acts 17 34|Act.17:34.]]† (AS)
Δαμασκηνός, -ή, -όν of Damascus, Damascene: [[2-corinthians 11 32|2Co.11:32.]]† (AS)
Δαμασκός, -οῦ, ἡ (Heb. דַּמֶּשֶׂק), Damascus: [[acts 9 2|Act.9.2ff. 22:5ff.26.12,20]], [[2-corinthians 11 32|2Co.11:32]], [[galatians 1 17|Gal.1:17]].† (AS)

δανίζω (late form of cl. -είζω, Rec., Bl., § 3; Thackeray, Gr., 85f.) [in LXX chiefly for לוה ([[proverbs 19 17|Pro.19:17]]) ;] to lend money on interest: [[luke 6 34|Luk.6:34, 35]]; mid., to borrow: [[matthew 5 42|Mat.5:42.]]† SYN.: κίχρημι (see: χράω), to lend in a friendly way. (AS)
δάνιον, -ου, τό (late form of δάνειον, Rec.; see: δανίζω), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 24 11|Deu.24:11]] (נָשָׁה) 15:8, 10 (עָבַט hi.), 4Ma.2:8 * ;] a loan: [[matthew 18 27|Mat.18:27.]]† (AS)

δανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (late form of -ειστής, Rec.; see: δανείζω), [in LXX: 4Ki.4:1, Psa.108(109):11 (נשׁה), [[proverbs 29 13|Pro.29:13]] (רָשׁ), Sir.29:28 * ;] a money-lender: [[luke 7 41|Luk.7:41.]]† (AS)
Δανιήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. דָּנִיֵּאל, God is my Judge), Daniel, the prophet: [[matthew 24 15|Mat.24:15.]]† (AS)

δαπανάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Tob.1:7, 1Ma.14:32, al. ;] 1. to spend, expend: with accusative, [[mark 5 26|Mrk.5:26;]] before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), [[acts 21 24|Act.21:24;]] ὑπέρ, [[2-corinthians 12 15|2Co.12:15.]] 2. to consume, squander: [[luke 15 14|Luk.15:14;]] ἐν τ. ἡδσναῖς (on the constr. with ἐν, see Hort, Mayor, in l.), [[james 4 3|Jas.4:3]] (cf. ἐκ-, προσ- δ.).† (AS)
δαπάνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: [[esther 6 4|Est.6:4]], 8 (נִפְקָא), Dan LXX Bel 1:21, al. ;] expense, cost: [[luke 14 28|Luk.14:28.]]† (AS)

δέ (before vowels δ᾽; on the general neglect of the elision in NT, see WH, App., 146; Tdf., Pr., 96), post-positive conjunctive particle; 1. copulative, but, in the next place, and, now (Abbott, JG, 104): [[matthew 1 2|Mat.1:2]]ff., [[2-corinthians 6 15|2Co.6:15, 16]], [[2-peter 1 5|2Pe.1:5-7]]; in repetition for emphasis, [[romans 3 21|Rom.3:21, 22, 9:30]], [[1-corinthians 2 6|1Co.2:6]], [[galatians 2 2|Gal.2:2]], [[philippians 2 8|Php.2:8]]; in transition to something new, [[matthew 1 18|Mat.1:18, 2:19]], [[luke 13 1|Luk.13:1]], [[john 7 14|Jhn.7:14]], [[acts 6 1|Act.6:1]], [[romans 8 28|Rom.8:28]], [[1-corinthians 7 1|1Co.7:1 8:1]], al.; in explanatory parenthesis or addition, [[john 3 19|Jhn.3:19]], [[romans 5 8|Rom.5:8]], [[1-corinthians 1 12|1Co.1:12]], [[ephesians 2 4|Eph.2:4, 5:32]], al.; ὡς δέ, [[john 2 9|Jhn.2:9;]] καὶ . . . δέ, but also, [[matthew 10 18|Mat.10:18]], [[luke 1 76|Luk.1:76]], [[john 6 51|Jhn.6:51]], [[romans 11 23|Rom.11:23]], al.; καὶ ἐὰν δέ, yea even if, [[john 8 16|Jhn.8:16.]] 2. Adversative, but, on the other hand, prop., answering to a foregoing μέν (which see), and distinguishing a word or clause from one preceding (in NT most frequently without μέν; Bl., §77, 12): ἐὰν δέ, [[matthew 6 14|Mat.6:14, 23]], al.; ἐγὼ (σὺ, etc.) δέ, [[matthew 5 22|Mat.5:22, 6:6]], [[mark 8 29|Mrk.8:29]], al.; ὁ δέ, αὐτὸς δέ, [[mark 1 45|Mrk.1:45]], [[luke 4 40|Luk.4:40]], al.; after a negation, [[matthew 6 19|Mat.6:19, 20]], [[romans 3 4|Rom.3:4]], [[1-thessalonians 5 21|1Th.5:21]], al. (AS)

δέησις, -εως, ἡ (δέομαι), [in LXX for תְּחִנָּה, רִנָּה, תְּפִלָּה, etc. ;] 1. a wanting, need (so [[psalms 22 25|Ps 21(22):25]]). 2. an asking, entreaty, supplica­tion; in NT always addressed to God: [[luke 1 13|Luk.1:13]], [[2-corinthians 1 11|2Co.1:11]], [[philippians 1 19|Php.1:19]], [[2-timothy 1 3|2Ti.1:3]], [[james 5 16|Jas.5:16]], [[1-peter 3 12|1Pe.3:12]]" (LXX) ; with νηστεῖαι, [[luke 2 37|Luk.2:37;]] προσυνχή, -αί, [[ephesians 6 18|Eph.6:18]], [[philippians 4 6|Php.4:6]], [[1-timothy 2 1|1Ti.2:1 5:5]]; ἱκετηρίαι, [[hebrews 5 7|Heb.5:7;]] προσκαρτέρησις, [[ephesians 6 18|Eph.6:18;]] ἐντεύξεις, [[1-timothy 2 1|1Ti.2:1;]] δ. ποιεῖσθαι (Deiss., BS, 250), [[luke 5 33|Luk.5:33]], [[philippians 1 4|Php.1:4]] (pl.), [[1-timothy 2 1|1Ti.2:1;]] before ὑπέρ, [[2-corinthians 9 14|2Co.9:14]], [[philippians 1 4|Php.1:4]]; περί, [[ephesians 6 18|Eph.6:18;]] πρός, [[romans 10 1|Rom.10:1.]]† SYN.: προσευχή, used of prayer in general, while δ. gives prominence to the sense of need; on the other hand, δ. is used as well of requests from man to man, while π. is limited to prayer to God. ἔντευξις, in the π., is the regular word for petition to a superior (Deiss., BS, 250; cf. the Pauline ἐντυγχάνειν, to entreat). Cf. also εὐχή. ([[james 5 15|Jas.5:15]]), αἴτημα, ἱκετηρία (Tr., Syn., § li; Cremer, 73, 174, 684). (AS)

δεῖ impersonal (δέω), [in LXX chiefly for infin. with לְ ;] one must, it is necessary: with inf., [[matthew 26 54|Mat.26:54]], [[mark 13 7|Mrk.13:7]], [[acts 5 29|Act.5:29]], al.; with accusative and inf., [[matthew 16 21|Mat.16:21]], [[mark 8 31|Mrk.8:31]], [[john 3 7|Jhn.3:7]], [[acts 25 10|Act.25:10]], al.; with ellipse of accusative, [[matthew 23 23|Mat.23:23;]] of accusative, and inf., [[mark 13 14|Mrk.13:14]], [[romans 1 27|Rom.1:27 8:26]]; οὐ (μὴ) δεῖ (non licet), ought not, must not: [[acts 25 24|Act.25:24]], [[2-timothy 2 24|2Ti.2:24]]; impf., ἔδει, of necessity or obligation in past time regarding a past event (Bl., § 63, 4), [[matthew 18 33|Mat.18:33]], [[luke 15 32|Luk.15:32]], [[john 4 4|Jhn.4:4]], [[acts 27 21|Act.27:21]], al.; periphr., δέον ἐστίν (as in Attic, χρεών ἐστι = χρή, see: δέον), [[acts 19 36|Act.19:36;]] id., with ellipse of ἐστίν, [[1-peter 1 6|1Pe.1:6]] τὰ μὴ δέοντα (= ἃ οὐ δεῖ [[1-timothy 5 13|1Ti.5:13.]] SYN.: ὀφείλει, expressing moral obligation, as distinct from δεῖ, denoting logical necessity and χρή, a need which results from the fitness of things (see Tr., Syn., § cvii, 10; Westc. on [[hebrews 2 1|Heb.2:1]], [[1-john 2 6|1Jn.2:6]]; Hort on [[james 3 10|Jas.3:10]]). (AS)
δεῖγμα, -τος, τό (δείκνυμι); 1. (cl.) a thing shown, a specimen. 2. = cl. παράδ- (cf. ὑπόδ-, [[2-peter 2 6|2Pe.2:6]]), an example (a warning): Ju 7.† (AS)
δειγματίζω (δεῖγμα), a rare word (ICC, ll. with), to make a show of, to expose: [[matthew 1 19|Mat.1:19]] (Rec. παραδ-, which see), [[colossians 2 15|Col.2:15.]]† (AS)

δείκνυμι, δεικνύω (see Bl., § 23, 1; Veitch, see word), [in LXX chiefly for רָאָה hi. ;] to show, with accusative of thing(s) (of person(s)), dative of person(s); (a) to show, exhibit: [[matthew 4 8|Mat.4:8 8:4]], [[mark 1 44|Mrk.1:44 14:15]], [[luke 4 5|Luk.4:5 5:14 20:24 22:12 24:40]], [[john 2 18|Jhn.2:18 5:20 10:32; 20:20]] [[acts 7 3|Act.7:3]]" (LXX), [[1-timothy 6 15|1Ti.6:15]], [[revelation 17 1|Rev.17:1 21:9, 10 22:1, 8]], pass., [[hebrews 8 5|Heb.8:5]] (LXX); (b) to make known: [[matthew 16 21|Mat.16:21]], [[john 14 8|Jhn.14:8]], 9, [[acts 10 28|Act.10:28]], [[1-corinthians 12 31|1Co.12:31]], [[revelation 1 1|Rev.1:1 4:1 22:6]]; (with) to prove: [[james 2 18|Jas.2:18 3:13]].† (AS)

δειλία, -ας, ἡ (δειλός), [in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc. ;] cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): [[2-timothy 1 7|2Ti.1:7.]]† SYN.: φόβος, fear, in general, good or bad; εὐλάβεια (which see), apprehension generally, but chiefly pious fear, "that careful and watchful reverence which pays regard to every circumstance in that with which it has to deal" (cf. Tr., Syn., § x).† (AS)
δειλιάω, -ῶ (δειλία), [in LXX for חתת ni., פּחד, etc. ;] = the more frequently ἀποδ-, to be cowardly, timid, fearful: [[john 14 27|Jhn.14:27.]]† (AS)
δειλός, -ή, όν (δέος), [in LXX for רַךְ, etc. ;] cowardly, fearful: [[matthew 8 26|Mat.8:26]], [[mark 4 40|Mrk.4:40]], [[revelation 21 8|Rev.21:8]].† (AS)

δεῖνα, ὁ, ἡ, τό (genitive -νος, dative -νι, accusative -να), [in Aq.: [[ruth 4 1|Rut.4:1]], [[1-samuel 21 2|1Ki.21:2]] (3) (Sm. also), [[2-kings 6 8|4Ki.6:8]] * ;] such an one, a certain one, whom one cannot or will not name: [[matthew 26 18|Mat.26:18.]]† (AS)
δεινῶς , adv. (δέος), [in LXX: [[job 10 16|Job.10:16]], Wis.17:3, al. ;] 1. terribly: [[matthew 8 6|Mat.8:6.]] 2. vehemently: [[luke 11 53|Luk.11:53.]]† (AS)

δειπνέω, -ῶ (δεῖπνον, which see), [in LXX: [[proverbs 23 1|Pro.23:1]] (לחם), Tob.7:8 8:1, Dan LXX 11:27 * ;] to take the chief meal of the day, to dine, to sup: [[luke 17 8|Luk.17:8 22:20]] (WH, br., R, mg. omits), [[1-corinthians 11 25|1Co.11:25;]] metaphorically, [[revelation 3 20|Rev.3:20.]]† (AS)

δεῖπνον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for פַּת־בַּג (Da) ;] the chief meal of the day, dinner, supper: [[matthew 23 6|Mat.23:6]], [[mark 12 39|Mrk.12:39]], [[luke 14 17|Luk.14:17, 24 20:46]], [[john 13 2|Jhn.13:2, 4 21:20]], [[1-corinthians 11 21|1Co.11:21]]; δ. ποιεῖν, [[mark 6 21|Mrk.6:21]], [[luke 14 12|Luk.14:12, 16]], [[john 12 2|Jhn.12:2]]; κυριακὸν (which see) δ., [[1-corinthians 11 20|1Co.11:20;]] metaphorically (Dalman, Words, 118), δ. τ. γάμου τ. ἀρνίου, [[revelation 19 9|Rev.19:9;]] δ. τ. μέγα τ. Θεοῦ, [[revelation 19 17|Rev.19:17.]]† (AS)

δεισι-δαίμων, -ον (δείδω, to fear; δαίμων, deity) reverent to the deity, religious; compar. -μονεστέρους (AV, too superstitious, R, txt., somewhat superstitious, a sense in wh. the word is sometimes used; cf. Field, Notes, 125), more religious, God fearing, than others, quite religious (Abbott, Essays, 105 ff.; Deiss., LAE, 285): [[acts 17 22|Act.17:22.]]† SYN.: εὐσεβής (which see), θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (Cremer, 681; DB, ext., 142 a). (AS)
δεισιδαιμονία, -ας, ἡ (δεισιδαίμων, which see); 1. fear of the gods; (a) piety, religion; (b) superstition. 2. Objectively, a religion: [[acts 25 19|Act.25:19]] (Cremer, 72, 682).† (AS)
δέκα, οἱ, αἱ, τά, ten: [[matthew 20 24|Mat.20:24]], al.; θλίψις ἡμερῶν δ., i.e. of brief duration: [[revelation 2 10|Rev.2:10.]]† δεκα-οκτώ, T for δέκα ὀκτώ, eighteen: [[luke 13 4|Luk.13:4.]]† (AS)
δεκα-δύω, Rec. for δώδεκα [[acts 19 7|Act.19:7 24:11]].† (AS)

δεκα-πέντε [in LXX: [[exodus 27 15|Exo.27:15]], 1Ma.10:40, al. ;] late form of πεντεκαίδεκα, fifteen: [[john 11 18|Jhn.11:18]], [[acts 27 5|Act.27:5]], WH, mg., ib. 28, [[galatians 1 18|Gal.1:18]].† (AS)
Δεκά-πολις, -εως, ὴ Decapolis, a region east of the Jordan con­taining ten cities: [[matthew 4 25|Mat.4:25]], [[mark 5 20|Mrk.5:20 7:31]].† (AS)

δεκατέσσαρες, -ων, oἱ, αἱ, -α, τά [in LXX: [[genesis 31 41|Gen.31:41]], Tob.8:19, al. ;] = cl. τεσσαρεσκαίδεκα, more frequently in later Gk. than the older form and in MGr. (for thirteen and upwards) universal, fourteen: [[matthew 1 17|Mat.1:17]], [[2-corinthians 12 2|2Co.12:2]], [[galatians 2 1|Gal.2:1]] (cf. τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος).† (AS)

δεκάτη, -ης, ἡ prop. fem. (sc. μέρος) of δέκατος, -η, -ον, [in LXX for מַעֲשֵׂר: [[genesis 14 20|Gen.14:20]], [[nehemiah 12 44|Neh.12:44]], and al. ;] a tenth part, a tithe: [[hebrews 7 2|Heb.7:2, 4; 8, 9]] (for a curious inversion of the Biblical use, see MM, see word).† (AS)
δέκατος, -η, -ον (δέκα), [in LXX for מַעֲשֵׂר and cognate forms ;] tenth: [[john 1 40|Jhn.1:40]], [[acts 19 9|Act.19:9]] (WH, txt., RV omit), [[revelation 11 13|Rev.11:13; 21:20]].† (AS)

δεκατόω, -ῶ, = cl. -τεύω (δεκάτη), [in LXX: [[nehemiah 10 37|Neh.10:37]] (38) (עשׂר pi.) * ;] to take tithe of: with accusative of person(s), [[hebrews 7 6|Heb.7:6;]] pass. to pay tithe: [[hebrews 7 9|Heb.7:9.]]† (AS)

δεκτός, -ή, -όν verbal adj. of δέχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for רָצוֹן: [[proverbs 11 1|Pro.11:1]], al. ;] acceptable: [[luke 4 19|Luk.4:19]] (LXX) 24, [[acts 10 35|Act.10:35]], [[2-corinthians 6 2|2Co.6:2]]" (LXX), [[philippians 4 18|Php.4:18]] (cf. εὐπροσδ-).† (AS)
δελεάζω (δέλεαρ, a bait), to allure by a bait: metaphorically, to allure, entice: with accusative, [[2-peter 2 14|2Pe.2:14, 18]]; pass., [[james 1 14|Jas.1:14.]]† (AS)

δένδρον, -ου, τό [in LXX for עֵץ, etc. ;] a tree: [[matthew 3 10|Mat.3:10]], al.; δ. ἀγαθόν, [[matthew 7 17|Mat.7:17, 18]]; δ. καλόν, [[matthew 12 33|Mat.12:33]], [[luke 6 43|Luk.6:43]]; δ. σαπρόν, [[matthew 7 17|Mat.7:17, 18 12:33]], [[luke 6 43|Luk.6:43]]; γίνεσθαι δ., [[matthew 13 32|Mat.13:32;]] γ. εἰς δ., [[luke 13 19|Luk.13:19.]] (AS)

δεξιολάβος, -ου, ὁ (δεξιός, λαμβάνω), a kind of soldier, prob. a spearman (Vg., lancearius) or slinger: [[acts 23 23|Act.23:23.]]† δεξιο-βόλος, -ου, ὁ (δεξιός, βάλλω), one who throws with the right hand: L for δεξιολάβος, [[acts 23 23|Act.23:23.]]† (AS)

[in LXX for חנן, etc. ;] to want for oneself; 1. to want, need: (a) absol.; (b) with genitive 2. to beg, request, beseech, pray; (i) in general: absol., [[acts 26 3|Act.26:3]], WH; with genitive of person(s), [[luke 5 12|Luk.5:12; 8:28; 38]] (ἐδεῖτο; T, ἐδέετο, cf.
